People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a text. You open any payments app, scan a code or pick a contact, enter your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds. There is no card to carry, no cash to count and no change to wait for.

It has also reached places cards never did. Small shops, tea stalls and vegetable sellers just need a printed QR code, not a machine. Since most people already have a phone and a bank account, there is little to set up, and one app can work with almost any bank.

Here are the three main reasons:

Free and fast: Most everyday payments between people and at shops cost nothing, and they arrive instantly, any time of day, even on holidays.
Simple and everywhere: One QR code or phone number works across apps and banks, from big stores to street vendors.
Feels safe: Every payment needs your PIN, you see the amount before you confirm, and your bank details stay hidden from the person you pay.

Together, these make UPI quicker than cash and easier than cards, so more people use it each year.
